title: Writing a file to Azure blob storage from synapse throws TASK_WRITE_FAILED
question:
I am creating some parquet files and I need to save them to an Azure blob storage. For this question I recreated the error trying to write a csv file out of a data frame.

I am working this script in an Azure Synapse Notebook. Reading and updating the files works ok. Reading is analogue to writing.

I used Pandas library to write files, at some point, and it worked ok. However, I run into issues with possible modification of the parquet file's scheme, so I went back to PySpark library.

Apparently, the issue could be permissions, thats why I include the relevant part of the sas token.

Writing Code python

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession

# Azure Storage configurations
storage_account_name = "<my-storage-account>"
container_name = "<my-container-name>"
sas_token = "<my-sas-token>ss=bfqt&srt=sco&sp=rwdlacupiytfx"

# Input and output paths
input_folder = "input"
output_folder = "output"

# Initialize Spark session
spark = SparkSession.builder.getOrCreate()

# Spark configuration for Azure Blob Storage
spark.conf.set(f"fs.azure.sas.{container_name}.{storage_account_name}.blob.core.windows.net", sas_token)

# Example DataFrame
test_df = spark.createDataFrame([(1, "test"), (2, "data")], ["id", "value"])
print("SCRIPT: data frame created")

# Write DataFrame to Azure Blob Storage
output_path = f"wasbs://{container_name}@{storage_account_name}.blob.core.windows.net/{output_folder}/test.csv"
print(f"SCRIPT: output path created: {output_path}")

print("SCRIPT: Writing data frame to the output path...")
# test_df.write.parquet(output_path).mode("overwrite")
test_df.write.mode("overwrite").csv(output_path)

print(f"SCRIPT: Data written successfully to {output_path}")

The code crashes at test_df.write.mode("overwrite").csv(output_path)

answer:
I have tried the below approach:

Initialize the connection to Azure Data Lake Storage (ADLS) in a Spark notebook:

spark.conf.set("fs.azure.account.key.allnewsynp.dfs.core.windows.net","<YOUR ACCESS KEY>")

You can find the access key In ADLS:

Code:

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
container_name = "synpdemocontainer"
storage_account_name = "allnewsynp"
output_folder = "output"
spark = SparkSession.builder.getOrCreate()
test_df = spark.createDataFrame([(1, "test"), (2, "data")], ["id", "value"])
output_path = f"abfss://{container_name}@{storage_account_name}.dfs.core.windows.net/{output_folder}/test.csv"
print(f"SCRIPT: output path created: {output_path}")
print("SCRIPT: Writing data frame to the output path...")
test_df.write.mode("overwrite").csv(output_path)
print(f"SCRIPT: Data written successfully to {output_path}")
